opinion.headline: Why the matinee remains cinema's quiet pleasure
opinion.hook: Escaping the midday heat for the cool, dark sanctuary of a cinema offers a unique rebellion.
opinion.summary: Inside, the world outside fades as the screen becomes a portal to imagined realms. This daytime retreat allows for complete immersion in stories, a glorious idleness that contrasts with the day's demands. Emerging, one carries the lingering magic of a fabricated reality, feeling more potent than the everyday world.

opinion.headline: When every story is breaking, none is
opinion.hook: The constant barrage of 'Breaking News' has lost its impact, with audiences now tuning out sensationalized headlines.
opinion.summary: Media outlets, once reliant on urgent alerts, find viewers have migrated online, where even significant events are met with indifference. This era of overused 'breaking' alerts has ended, leaving traditional news channels struggling to capture attention in a fragmented media landscape. The only real 'breaking' news now seems to be found in entertainment.

opinion.headline: Building resilient supply chains through an India-Chile partnership
opinion.hook: Chile, a major global player in critical minerals like copper and lithium, presents a compelling strategic alliance opportunity for India.
opinion.summary: Beyond resource extraction, the partnership aims to integrate value chains for AI and data center inputs. Chile's stable economy, robust legal framework, and attractive investment incentives, including R&D tax credits and a new business visa system, make it an ideal partner for India's energy security and decarbonization goals.

opinion.headline: The Divine Flow
opinion.hook: The writer recalls how her mother used to take a self-declared three-day "vacation" during menstruation, avoiding household work and spending time reading and drawing.
opinion.summary: While such menstrual seclusion practices have largely disappeared and are now seen as outdated, the author notes that ancient traditions also viewed menstruation as sacred and life-affirming, citing the Ambubachi Mela at Assam's Kamakhya Temple, which celebrates the goddess's annual menstrual cycle.
